title: Leeds’ Ilia Gruev out for rest of season with meniscus injury
content:
Leeds United midfielder Ilia Gruev has been ruled out for the rest of the season after suffering a meniscus injury in training.

The Bulgaria international was absent from Wednesday’s 2-2 draw with Bournemouth in the Premier League and manager Daniel Farke confirmed on Thursday his season is over.

Gruev, 25, had not been in the starting line-up since March 3, but has always been a trusted lieutenant for Farke in the engine room. The manager hopes to have him back for the start of pre-season, while right-back Jayden Bogle has a chance of shaking off the knock he picked up in Dorset last night.

“Sadly, it’s bad news with Ilia Gruev,” Farke told reporters at a press conference ahead of Sunday’s FA Cup semi-final against Chelsea. “Meniscus injury is confirmed. It will keep him definitely out for the whole season, so he won’t be able to help us for the run-in, not in the FA Cup and also not in the league.

“We expect to have him back for the start of pre-season, but he won’t feature during this season anymore. It’s, of course, not ideal for us and we all feel for him.

“Jayden Bogle got a hit against this foot (last night). It seems not to be too bad. We have to wait to see how quickly he can recover and I hope to have him available for the game on Sunday.”

Anton Stach has missed the last three matches with an ankle ligament injury. The midfielder is yet to return to team training, but Farke said he will be given every chance to return for the Wembley showpiece, such is his importance to the team.

“(He’s) not yet in team training, but we have a few more days,” he said. “We will see. The first step is to have him back in team training, rather sooner than later.

“If a key player like him would be back in team training, then he has a chance to be picked because he’s a crucial player for us. Let’s see how the next 72 hours will develop.”

Sebastiaan Bornauw was an unused substitute for Leeds at Bournemouth, but he rolled his ankle in the pre-match warm-up. Therefore, he missed training at Thorp Arch on Thursday, but could yet be a factor on Sunday, too.

“During the warm-up, he rolled his ankle and this was not ideal,” he said. “Yesterday, it was pretty sore. Today, he was not able to join us in team training, but I hope it’s not too bad. At least it seems there is no ligament injury.

“I hope to have him back in training tomorrow and if he’s back in training, then he would also be available.”
